subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 3 – Lesson 6: Culture and Project – Ancient cities in our region
outcomes: I can understand facts about Baalbek, Carthage and Petra.
I can say what old buildings tell us about the past.
I can make and present a tourist brochure about an ancient city.

tf.why: Baalbek is an ancient city in Lebanon.
Carthage is in Tunisia; Petra is in Jordan.

tf.s: Baalbek is more than 2,000 years old.
tf.why: It is a very old, ancient city.

tf.s: Carthage was an important harbour on the coast of Tunisia.
tf.why: Boats came to its harbour on the coast.

tf.s: There is a new theatre in Petra today.
tf.why: The theatre in Petra is ancient, not new.

tf.s: In Petra, people bought and sold spices.
tf.why: Spices came from India, China and Egypt.

tf.s: Today you can see Roman baths, statues and a theatre in Carthage.
tf.why: You can also see the city walls.

tf.s: Ruins are buildings that are brand new.
tf.why: Ruins are what is left of old, broken buildings.

tf.s: A good brochure has headings, pictures and short texts.
tf.why: These help visitors find information quickly.

boxes.why: Baalbek is more than 2,000 years old.

boxes.q: What did people buy and sell in Petra?
boxes.why: They traded spices from India, China and Egypt.
Carthage was a harbour on the coast.

boxes.q: Complete: Jerash is a city which is more than ___ years old.
boxes.why: Jerash is more than 2,000 years old.

boxes.q: Which is an ancient place in Oman?
boxes.why: Bat is in Oman; the others are in other countries.

boxes.q: Why should you speak in a loud, clear voice?
o: So everyone can hear and understand.
boxes.why: A clear voice helps your audience.

boxes.q: Which phrase can you use in your brochure?
boxes.why: Today you can see … tells visitors what is there.

boxes.q: Complete: Why don’t we visit Petra? – Good ___.
boxes.why: Good idea! agrees with a suggestion.

hunt.q: The land next to the sea
Baalbek is more than ___ years old

mcq.q: What can you still see in Carthage today?
o: city walls, Roman baths, statues and a theatre
mcq.why: These ancient things are still there.

mcq.q: Where did the spices in Petra come from?
mcq.why: Traders brought spices from India, China and Egypt.

mcq.q: Which three things should your project notes include?
o: how old the city is, the most important buildings, what you can see today
your name, age and phone number
mcq.why: These are the three parts of the notes.

mcq.q: Which three cities are in the culture texts?
mcq.why: The texts are about Baalbek, Carthage and Petra.

mcq.q: Choose the best sentence for a brochure.
o: The most important building is the Roman theatre.
The most important building is my bedroom.
Could you show me the theatre?
mcq.why: It uses a project phrase and gives useful information.

mcq.q: Write about Bahla Fort. Which sentence is best?
o: Bahla Fort is very old and you can see its walls and towers.
Bahla Fort is a new shopping mall.
Bahla Fort was built last year.
mcq.why: It describes an old building in Oman correctly.

mcq.q: “Carthage is in Lebanon.” True, false or doesn’t say?

o: It was a harbour on the coast, so boats and trade came there.
It was in the middle of the desert.
mcq.why: A harbour city connects people by sea.

mcq.q: What do old buildings in our town tell us?
o: How people lived in the past
What the weather will be tomorrow
mcq.why: Old buildings show us our history.

mcq.q: Petra had people from many places buying and selling spices. What does this tell us?
o: Petra was an important place for trade.
Petra was a small, quiet village.
mcq.why: Trade from many countries means it was an important city.
